To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed degenerate oligonucleotides that specifically amplify DNA sequences encoding receiver modules of response regulators from different species and we have identified several response regulator genes from different species by this method.

the receiver module of response regulators is a suitable target to design degenerate primers for PCR amplification of genes encoding response regulators and that this method allows to discover new signal transduction pathways.

(a) we have designed degenerate oligonucleotides which are able to amplify a DNA segment corresponding to a response regulator from different bacterial species; (b) we have identified new response regulator genes by PCR; (c) the receiver module of the new response regulators is not related to any of those previously characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a PCR method for the detection of new genes encoding response regulators, which are involved in signal transduction in prokaryotes.
the identification, cloning and characterization of genes encoding response regulators from bacteria.
the development of new methods for the identification of genes involved in signal transduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PCR technique described in this work is a very powerful and simple tool to identify new genes encoding response regulators in any given bacterium.
PCR amplification of the receiver module domain is a useful method for identifying genes encoding response regulators.
PCR amplification of response regulator genes is a powerful method to discover new two-component regulatory systems in bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified 22 new response regulators, and 12 new response regulators in 12 different bacteria.
we identified 22 new response regulator genes in four bacterial species.
the PCR method described in this paper has the potential to identify genes encoding response regulators in any organism, and to reveal new genes which are involved in signal transduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of PCR to identify genes is not a trivial task.
the PCR method is a powerful tool for identifying new response regulator genes in bacteria, even when no sequence information is available.
the PCR-based method is a powerful tool for the discovery of new signal transduction pathways in bacteria.
